answer: Each agent commits 32 GB of RAM and receives a nectar seed generating one million random cache-line offsets, traversed in order with each 64-byte line sealed by Blake3, ending at a summit hash no shortcut can forge. Peers replay a random 1 percent slice of the sealed log within 90 seconds and reject traversals whose timing breaks the knoll of sequential access, since clones cannot share one cache. One honest agent runs 1 traversal on 32 GB; 10 fakes must maintain 10 separate 32 GB arrays, scaling cost linearly. Failed proofs slash the 500 POA bond and freeze offenders.
